contract.reader: An engineering student or engineer who has met transfer functions and poles (the series' first entry) and wants to see concretely what closing a loop changes
contract.problem: Knowing what proportional feedback buys and what it costs, instead of assuming that feedback simply makes the output correct
contract.outcome: Compute the closed-loop pole, time constant and offset of a first-order loop; show that feedback can stabilize an unstable plant and state the minimum gain; explain the 1/(1 + L0) reduction of sensitivity and disturbance effect; name what limits the gain
contract.contribution: The smallest model that shows every effect, with one factor 1/(1 + L0) tying offset, disturbance rejection and sensitivity together, checked by a standard-library simulation, and the explicit point that on the nominal plant feedback does not improve accuracy
contract.evidence: Algebra in the text; two Python scripts with their quoted output; Astrom and Murray (2021); Franklin, Powell and Emami-Naeini (2019); the sampled-loop limit of the digital-control entry
contract.limitations: First-order, continuous-time, proportional only; delay, saturation and noise are quantified but not modeled; integral action deferred

findings.location: Sections 1.1, 2.3 and 2.4, display equations (360 px; mobile-light-03, 06, 08)
findings.problem: Each display is wider than the column; its right end (b > 0; most of the error formula; /b = 1) is hidden behind an unmarked sideways scroll
findings.whyItMatters: Small: results are restated nearby, but the 2.4 condition is the subsection's conclusion
findings.action: Break the three displays for narrow screens, or add a site-level scroll cue for wide equations
findings.acceptance: On new 360 px captures all three displays are fully visible, or a visible cue shows that they scroll

findings.location: Section 2.1 loop diagram and Section 2.3 step-response plot (360 px; mobile-light-04, 07)
findings.problem: Generated figures keep a 26rem minimum width, so the right fifth is hidden: the output x of the loop and all curve labels and the axis label of the plot; the caption does not name the line styles
findings.whyItMatters: On a phone the step-response plot becomes four unnamed curves
findings.action: Site-level scroll cue for wide figures; labels inside the plot area or a caption naming the line styles
findings.acceptance: At 360 px the curve labels are visible or the caption identifies each line style, and the loop output is visible or visibly scrollable

findings.problem: Axis labeled 'time t' without a unit
findings.whyItMatters: Standards 6.8 chart integrity requires units; the reader compares time constants by eye here
findings.action: Label the axis 'time t (s)' in scripts/generate-diagrams.py and regenerate
findings.acceptance: The axis reads 'time t (s)' on the live page

findings.location: Section 4.1 disturbance paragraph (desktop-light-06); Section 5 noise item (mobile-light-16)
findings.problem: Lines break between an inline equation and the following full stop, so a line begins with a period
findings.whyItMatters: Polish; looks like an error. Site-wide cause (KaTeX output followed by punctuation)
findings.action: Site level: keep trailing punctuation with the preceding inline equation
findings.acceptance: No line on the page begins with a period or comma at 1280 or 360 px
